# CharlieHub Control Manager (CCM)

**Lifecycle:** REFERENCE
<!-- lifecycle: REFERENCE -->


## What CCM Is

The **CharlieHub Control Manager (CCM)** is not a new service — it is the unified governance contract over all CharlieHub control-plane components. It enforces that every persistent network and routing entity follows the same invariants: DB as source of truth, API as sole write path, generator as the only artifact writer, and explicit lifecycle state on every entity.

CCM exists because the control plane has organically grown five distinct managers that share a single PostgreSQL instance and a single Traefik/nftables execution plane. Without a common contract, each manager invents its own state model, its own API patterns, and its own generator discipline — creating invisible coupling and drift.

## Component Map

| CCM Component | Current Name | Manages | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ccm-domain | Domain Manager | HTTP/TCP routes, TLS, DDNS | Active (v3) |
| ccm-transit | Transit Manager | WireGuard peers, policy routing, NAT | Active (v3) |
| ccm-docs | Docs Manager | MkDocs pages and nav | Active (v2) |
| ccm-lan | LAN Manager | DHCP assignments, dnsmasq config | Active (v1) |
| ccm-edge | CCM Edge | Gateway configs, interfaces, edge enforcement | Operational (endpoints live; migration 035 applied; Paris nic1 multi-address realized) |

Each component is a separate service with its own API surface. CCM provides the contract they all implement — not an additional layer they call through.

## CCM Invariants

These five invariants are non-negotiable across all CCM components.

**I-1 — DB is the only source of truth.**
All persistent state lives in PostgreSQL on hub2. No file on any execution node is authoritative. If a file disagrees with the DB, the file is wrong.

**I-2 — The API is the only write path.**
No agent, operator, or automated process writes to execution-plane files directly. The only sanctioned mutation path is an API call to the relevant ccm-* component. The API enforces constraints, tracks revisions, and emits audit events.

**I-3 — Generators overwrite entirely, and exactly one component owns each artifact path.**
When a generator runs, it rewrites its target artifact from scratch from DB state. It never patches, merges, or appends. At any point in time, exactly one CCM component is the writer for a given artifact path — all others are read-only observers. This constraint is enforced via `ccm.artifacts` (see below).

**I-4 — Deploy can lag; DB commit cannot be rolled back by runtime.**
Once a DB record is committed, it is the new truth. A generator may not have run yet — that is a deploy lag, not a conflict. The runtime state of an execution node is always "catching up to DB". Never modify DB to match broken runtime.

**I-5 — Every entity has an explicit lifecycle state.**
No entity exists in an ambiguous implicit state. Every record in every ccm.* table carries a `state` column from the standard state model below.

## Standard State Model

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Created in DB, no artifact generated yet. Safe to mutate or delete. |
| `active` | Generated and deployed to execution plane. In service. |
| `inactive` | Was active, now intentionally stopped. Artifact removed or interface down. |
| `planned` | Modelled in DB, intentionally not deployed yet. Execution plane ignores it. |

`planned` is critical for entities that are configured but deliberately not running — for example, wg-ad on ch-transit-core, which is modelled in DB with a port DNAT in place but whose interface will not be brought up until the AD site is ready.

**Component extensions:** individual components may add terminal states beyond this base model. ccm-domain adds `disabled` — a terminal variant of `inactive` with no resurrection path. Component-specific extensions are documented in the component's own reference, not here.

## Standard API Contract

Every ccm-* component exposes this API shape. Component-specific fields are additive — the base contract does not change.

| Method | Path | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/ccm/{module}` | Create entity in `draft` state. Returns `id`, `revision=1`, `ETag: "1"`. |
| `POST` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}/activate` | Validate dependency graph and mark entity eligible for generation. Transitions `draft` → `active`. Does **not** write to execution plane. |
| `POST` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}/deploy` | Run generator and push artifacts to execution plane. Entity must be `active`. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}` | Update mutable fields. Requires `If-Match: "{revision}"`. Returns new `ETag`. |
| `GET` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}` | Fetch entity. Returns `ETag` header. |
| `GET` | `/api/ccm/{module}` | List all entities with filtering. |
| `POST` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}/disable` | Transition to `inactive`. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/ccm/{module}/{id}` | Hard delete. Only allowed in `draft` state. |

**Activate ≠ Deploy.** Activation validates the logical model (all required fields present, dependencies resolved, no conflicting resource claims) and marks the entity ready. Deployment runs the generator and writes artifacts. These are always two separate operations — never merged into one.

Lifecycle transitions (`draft→active`, `active→inactive`) are always explicit `POST` actions — never implicit side-effects of a `PATCH`.

## Logical Model → Artifact → Runtime

CCM components work in four distinct layers. Confusing layers is the most common source of drift.

```
DB (ccm.* tables)
  └─ logical model: what should exist and why
       └─ ccm.artifacts: which file path, which owner, which template
            └─ generator: renders artifact from logical model
                 └─ execution plane: runtime state on the edge node
```

**Logical model** is the intent: "px5 should SNAT traffic from 10.35.50.0/24 to the WAN interface." It says nothing about iptables or nftables.

**Artifact** is the file or config block that encodes that intent: `/etc/network/interfaces.d/wg-site-hooks.cfg`. It is owned by exactly one component and one template.

**Generator** decides the rendering: which backend (iptables/nftables), which syntax, which file format. Generators are the only layer that knows about implementation specifics.

**Runtime** is what the execution node actually has loaded. It should match the artifact. If it doesn't, that is drift.

## Artifact Ownership

`ccm.artifacts` is the ownership registry. Every generated file on every execution node must have exactly one row here.

```sql
CREATE TABLE ccm.artifacts (
    id                      SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    edge_id                 INTEGER REFERENCES ccm.edges(id),
    path                    TEXT NOT NULL,          -- absolute path on the edge node
    owner                   TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'ccm_edge' | 'transit_manager' | 'ccm_domain' | etc.
    managed                 BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,  -- false = tracked but not generated
    template                TEXT,                   -- generator template name
    last_generated_revision INTEGER,                -- revision at last deploy
    state                   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                                CHECK (state IN ('active','inactive')),
    notes                   TEXT,
    UNIQUE (edge_id, path)
);
```

A generator checks `ccm.artifacts` before writing. If the path is owned by a different component, the generator aborts rather than overwrite. `managed=false` entries are tracked for drift detection but never written by any generator — they are `manual` or `proxmox_native` artifacts.

**Populating the registry — `register_from_render` (deployed 2026-07-12).** Rows were originally hand-seeded per edge during bring-up — one `POST /api/ccm/edge/edges/{id}/artifacts` call per path, the pattern used to commission Andorra's Phase 0. `POST /api/ccm/edge/edges/{edge_id}/artifacts/register-from-render` now derives the same rows directly from the generator's `render()` owned-set: one `owner='ccm_edge', managed=true` row per rendered path, **CREATE-only** (`ON CONFLICT (edge_id, path) DO NOTHING`), fully idempotent. The gate itself is unchanged — a foreign-owned or deliberately `managed=false` path still (correctly) 409s the deploy guard — only the registry's *upkeep* is now generator-derived instead of hand-maintained, so a first-of-its-kind edge no longer has to hit an empty-registry wall before its first deploy. **Validated live on hub2, 2026-07-12** against the Andorra edge (`ccm.edges` id 12, `ad1-and-edge`): `registered: []`, `already_present` = the full Phase-0 hand-seeded set (`nat.rules`, `mangle.rules`, `routing-tables.sh`, `wg-site-hooks.sh`) — zero delta, confirming the generator-derived allowlist exactly reproduces what was hand-seeded. See `programme/sdwan-v4.5/drafts/edge-convergence-refactor.md` in the repo for the full design rationale and rollout tracker (Phase 3 fleet staging still pending).

## DB Schema Convention

All CCM tables live in the `ccm` PostgreSQL schema on hub2. Pre-CCM tables (`domains`, `dns_records`, etc.) keep their existing schema and are not migrated.

```sql
-- Base pattern for all ccm.* tables
CREATE TABLE ccm.<entity> (
    id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    revision    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    state       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
                    CHECK (state IN ('draft','active','inactive','planned')),
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    -- entity-specific columns follow
);
```

Revision increments on every PATCH. ETag is always the revision as a quoted integer string.

## Generator Discipline

Every CCM generator follows this 7-step process:

1. **Read** — fetch all `active` + `planned` records for this generator's scope from the logical model tables
2. **Validate** — assert the fetched records form a coherent set (no conflicting resources, no missing dependencies)
3. **Check ownership** — verify `ccm.artifacts` for every target path; abort if any path is owned by another component
4. **Render** — produce the complete target artifact in memory from the logical model; do not embed backend specifics in the logical layer
5. **Stamp** — prepend `# Generated by <component> — revision <max_revision> — <timestamp>` header
6. **Atomic write** — write via temp file + rename; never truncate-in-place
7. **Signal** — notify the consuming service (`systemd reload`, `wg syncconf`, etc.)

Generators never read their own output as input. They never merge with existing file content. The choice of rendering backend (iptables vs nftables, wg-quick vs ifupdown2) lives in the generator, not the logical model.

## What CCM Does Not Do

- CCM does **not** merge all managers into one service. They remain separate processes.
- CCM does **not** require renaming existing working components immediately. Rename happens when a component is refactored to implement the full CCM contract.
- CCM does **not** add a routing layer between components. Components still own their own APIs.
- CCM does **not** apply to services outside hub2. Edge nodes (px5, px1, transit-core) are the execution plane — they receive generated artifacts and do not run CCM logic.
- CCM is **not** Kubernetes or a service mesh. It is a naming and discipline contract, not infrastructure.

## Current Component Status

| ccm-domain | Full | I-1 I-2 I-3 I-4 I-5 | Full (draft/active/inactive/disabled) | No | Render + drift endpoints. Prometheus metrics (`artifact_matches_db`, `last_render_timestamp`). Deploy post-condition. Gaps 1, 5 resolved. |
| ccm-transit | Partial | I-1 I-2 I-3 | Missing | No | wg-ad demonstrates need for `planned`; wg-rw.conf is hand-managed |
| ccm-docs | Complete | I-1 I-2 I-3 I-5 | Full (draft/active/inactive/archived) | No | All CCM-applicable invariants met. Render, drift, metrics, generator stamp, atomic deploy. Runbook system retired. |
| ccm-lan | Partial | I-1 I-2 I-3 | Missing | No | Active service (`charliehub_ccm_lan`). FR scopes plus UK `10.<locality>.4.0/24` consumer scopes. VLAN 50 retired 2026-05-04; px5 is compute-only (no LAN scope). Generator pushes dnsmasq config via SSH. No CCM state model — uses `enabled` boolean on reservations instead. No ETag/revision on reservations. No artifact registry. |
| ccm-edge | Operational | — | — | — | Endpoints live; migration 035 applied; Paris nic1 multi-address realized (I-INTERFACE-REALIZATION-1). See CCM Network & Edge |

# Agent Guides

**Lifecycle:** REFERENCE

Documentation for agents and developers operating CharlieHub infrastructure.

## CCM — Five Control-Plane APIs

CharlieHub's control plane is governed by **[CCM — CharlieHub Control Manager](../control-plane/foundational/ccm.md)**. CCM is not a service — it is the contract that all control-plane components implement. Each has its own API. **None can be bypassed.**

| CCM Component | What you're changing | API |
|---|---|---|
| **ccm-domain** | Routing, domains, TLS, Traefik | Domain Manager (`localhost:8001`) |
| **ccm-transit** | WireGuard peers, nftables, NAT | Transit Manager (`localhost:8010`) |
| **ccm-docs** | Documentation pages and nav | Docs API (`docs-api.charliehub.net`) |
| **ccm-lan** | DHCP reservations, dnsmasq | LAN Manager (`localhost:8047`) |
| **ccm-edge** | Gateway configs, interfaces, NAT rules | Deployed via ccm-transit + ccm-edge generator |

---

## Golden Rule

**The control plane is authoritative. Files are not.**

- ❌ Never edit Traefik configs, routes.yml, or any generated file
- ❌ Never edit `.md` files directly or modify `mkdocs.yml`
- ❌ Never write directly to the database
- ✅ Always use the appropriate API
- ✅ Always use `If-Match` when updating existing resources
- ✅ Always run the relevant deploy after changes

---

## Guides

### Start Here

**[Start Here →](start-here.md)** — Which API do I need? Quick orientation for new agents.

### Domain Manager API (ccm-domain)

**[API Guide →](api-guide.md)** — Complete reference for routing, domains, TLS, and middleware.

### Transit Manager API (ccm-transit)

**[Transit Manager →](../services/transit-manager.md)** — WireGuard peers, nftables policy routing, NAT, SD-WAN topology.

### Docs API (ccm-docs)

**[Docs API →](docs-api.md)** — Create, update, and deploy documentation pages via API.

### Troubleshooting

**[Troubleshooting →](troubleshooting.md)** — Error codes, diagnostics, and common fixes.

---

## Key Principles

1. **Database is the source of truth** — generated files are derived state
2. **All changes go through the API** — validation, audit, and rollback only work this way
3. **Optimistic locking is mandatory** — always `GET` revision before `PUT`
4. **Deploy is a separate step** — changes don't go live until you deploy
5. **If the API can't express it, extend the API** — never bypass it

---

## Executive Summary

CharlieHub is a distributed infrastructure spanning three geographic
locations (UK homelab, France homelab, OVH datacenter) plus a dedicated
customer-platform VPS, connected by a WireGuard transit fabric routed
through a dedicated transit VM (**ch-transit-core**).

Two hosts carry distinct, deliberately-separated roles:

- **hub2** (OVH dedicated) is the **core CharlieHub control plane, documentation,
  and internal-services hub**. It runs the single Traefik ingress, the CCM
  control-plane APIs (Domain Manager, Transit Manager, ccm-lan), Authelia SSO,
  the docs platform, monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana), mail, and the platform
  MCP. It owns and coordinates the **Proxmox homelab** (px1/px2/px3 UK, px5 FR)
  and the SD-WAN edges (uk-edge-1, fr-edge-1, paris-pi4) through the transit
  fabric. It does **not** host customer product workloads — with one decommissioning
  exception, the former CBRE occupancy pipeline (see below): its reads cut over to
  the Trevarn platform on 2026-07-19 and hub2 ingest was cut on 2026-07-28, leaving
  the hub2 stack idle pending Phase 4 teardown.

- **vps3** (OVH VPS) is the **customer-facing Trevarn platform for client
  projects**. The Trevarn platform is the converged multi-tenant home for
  CharlieHub's IoT client work — currently **occupancy** (CBRE / `microshare.eu`)
  and **parking** (`verdegris.eu`) — backed by a self-hosted ChirpStack LNS
  (`cs-prod`), real LoRaWAN gateways, and the converged ingestion / worker /
  platform-API stack.

The separation is the point: hub2 is *control plane + internal*; vps3 is
*customer product*. Runtime placement is evidence, not authority — ownership
is defined by the control plane, not by which host a container happens to run on.

**SD-WAN v4 (2026-05-04 UK / 2026-05-11 FR):** uk-edge-1 (Dell OptiPlex 3050,
Debian 12) is the UK site gateway; fr-edge-1 (Dell OptiPlex, Dinard, 10.35.1.1)
is the FR site gateway (commissioned 2026-05-11; px5 is now compute-only at Le
Mans). UCGs are powered off and out of all data paths. px1/px2/px3 are compute
members only — no wg-site, no gateway role. See [SD-WAN Architecture](../sdwan.md).

## Core Components

### 1. Unified Traefik (Single Instance — ACME Only)
**Location:** hub2 | **Container:** `charliehub-traefik` (Traefik v3)
**Ports:** 80 (HTTP redirect), 443 (HTTPS), 8883 (TCP entrypoint)
**Certificates:** ACME production (Let's Encrypt)
**Architecture:** Single-writer (drift-proof), file-based routes generated from the
Domain Manager database.

- ✅ ACME certificate management (auto-renewal)
- ✅ Public DNS routing (`*.charliehub.net`, `*.verdegris.eu`, etc.)
- ✅ Authelia SSO integration (middleware fails closed → HTTP 403)
- ✅ Domain Manager API-driven (no Docker labels, no manual YAML)
- ✅ Drift-proof (single source of truth: PostgreSQL)

The `:8883` TCP entrypoint historically fronted the hub2 parking MQTT broker
(`mqtt.verdegris.eu` → `parking-mosquitto`). With parking moved to vps3, the
gateways now talk **directly to `cs-prod` on vps3** (UDP :1700); the hub2 MQTT
TCP route is retired. Route generation flow: see
[Traefik](../../services/traefik.md#how-traefik-domain-manager-work-together).

### 2. ccm-domain — Domain Manager Control Plane
**Location:** hub2 | **Container:** `charliehub_domain_manager_v3` | **Port:** 8001
**Database:** PostgreSQL 16 (`charliehub_domains`)

- PostgreSQL `domains` table is the source of truth
- API validates all changes before persisting (11 CHECK constraints, 7 ENUMs, trigger functions)
- Generator (`traefik_generator.py`) converts database → YAML routes
- Manages DDNS via OVH API; user provisioning writes `users_database.yml`

**Optimistic locking:** all `PUT /api/domains/{id}` require an `If-Match` ETag from `GET`.

```bash
curl -i -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" http://localhost:8001/api/domains/42   # returns ETag
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8001/api/domains/42 \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H 'If-Match: "abc123"' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"backend_port": 9000}'
```

!!! warning "Always use static IPs for `backend_host`"
    Never use an FQDN for a Domain Manager `backend_host` — it routes the request
    back through Traefik and creates a loop.

### 3. ccm-transit — Transit Manager Control Plane
**Location:** hub2 | **Container:** `charliehub_transit_manager` | **Port:** 8010
(also `https://tm-internal.charliehub.net`, X-API-Key, no Authelia)
**Database:** PostgreSQL 16 (`charliehub_domains` → `transit.*` schema)

Owns all WireGuard configs, nftables rules, and routing policy for
ch-transit-core — the networking equivalent of the Domain Manager:

```
transit.* tables (PostgreSQL)
  → Transit Manager API (/api/transit/*)   ← only writer
  → transit_generator.py (reads DB, loads keys from VM)
  → SSH push to ch-transit-core (10.0.0.2):
      /etc/wireguard/wg-{name}.conf
      /etc/nftables.d/generated/transit.nft
      /etc/systemd/system/transit-routing.service.d/generated.conf
```

Peer lifecycle (`draft → active → disabled`) with atomic `wg syncconf`; dry-run
deploys; primary-inversion guard; rollback snapshots in `deploy_log`; dual deploy
lock; 30s drift monitor (17 metrics / 17 alert rules). **Deploy — two live paths:** (1) `POST /api/transit/deploy {scope, dry_run}` — the S1 **scoped** deploy (live since 2026-05-28), the **sole writer of `transit.edge_node_status`**; always dry-run first (`dry_run: true`). (2) `scripts/deploy-transit.sh` — the full-fabric two-step path. (The per-node `/deploy/edge/{id}` stub is retired.) See [Transit Manager](../../services/transit-manager.md).

### 4. WireGuard Transit Fabric

All WireGuard tunnel termination runs inside **ch-transit-core** (VM at 10.0.0.2
on `br-transit`). Hub2 connects to it via a `/30` bridge; the VM runs nftables
and policy routing to forward traffic between all fabric participants. UCGs are
powered off (SD-WAN v4); uk-edge-1 / fr-edge-1 are the site gateways.

**ch-transit-core interfaces:**
```
wg-uk        10.244.44.1/30    uk-edge-1 (10.244.44.6) — UK SD-WAN v4 gateway
wg-fr        10.244.35.1/30    fr-edge-1 (10.244.35.2) — FR SD-WAN v4 gateway
wg-paris     10.244.75.1/30    paris-pi4-wg-gw (10.244.75.2)
wga-usa      10.244.215.1/30   Philadelphia UCG Ultra — US GEO exit (B2 client)
wg-rw        10.244.250.1/24   Road warriors (split / GEO / full-tunnel)
wg-outpost   10.244.251.1/24   Tenant egress (internet-only)
wg-infra     10.244.200.1/30   Infrastructure nodes (vps3 = .200.2)
enp1s0       10.0.0.2          br-transit link to hub2 (10.0.0.1)
```

**Road-warrior GEO routing (policy tables):**
```
10.244.250.0/26    Split-tunnel P1  — LAN access only
10.244.250.64/26   UK GEO           — exit via wg-uk → uk-edge-1, MASQUERADE
10.244.250.128/26  FR GEO           — exit via wg-fr → fr-edge-1, MASQUERADE
10.244.250.192/26  US GEO           — exit via wga-usa (Philadelphia)
```

**Firewall:** nftables (`table inet transit`) — managed exclusively by Transit
Manager (never edit manually). **Hub2 transit NAT:** pure nftables `ch_transit`
table — Docker is structurally irrelevant to it (a `docker restart` cannot affect
it). **Hub2 routing:** `10.44/16`, `10.35/16`, `10.75/16`, `10.244/16` all `via 10.0.0.2 dev br-transit`.

**vps3 fabric membership:** connected via `wg-infra` (10.244.200.2); routes to all
site LANs installed automatically; backup L2 path vps3 → wg-infra → wg-uk → px1.

### 5. Security Hardening

```
File permissions   Python 444 · config 440 · dirs 555 · .env 440
Firewall           hub2 Docker NAT: iptables (Docker daemon)
                   hub2 transit NAT: nftables ch_transit (Docker-independent)
                   ch-transit-core: nftables table inet transit (Transit Manager)
                   vps3: UFW (443 + WireGuard only)
Pre-commit hooks   block API keys / passwords / JWTs; no --no-verify
Secret rotation    quarterly (last Sunday @ 02:00 UTC)
```

All hub2 containers run `cap_drop: ALL` + `no-new-privileges:true`;
`docker.sock` is not mounted in application containers — Docker API access is
mediated by `docker-socket-proxy`.

## Key Infrastructure Decisions

### Decision: Single Traefik + ACME-Only Model
Consolidated the previous dual-Traefik (public + internal CA) model to a single
ACME-only instance: eliminated internal-CA complexity, unified certificate
management, moved internal services to file-based routes with IP-allowlist
middleware (fails closed → 403), zero domain renames.

### Decision: SD-WAN v3/v4 — UCGs Out of Data Path
UniFi firmware unconditionally NATs site-to-site traffic (`MASQUERADE -o wgclt+`),
breaking Corosync/Ceph. v3 made Proxmox hosts the gateways; v4 (2026-05) replaced
them with dedicated edge nodes (uk-edge-1, fr-edge-1). UCGs powered off — no
watchdog scripts, no cron, no MASQUERADE on site-to-site traffic by design.

### Decision: Separate control plane (hub2) from customer platform (vps3)
Customer IoT product workloads belong on the **Trevarn platform on vps3**, not on
the control-plane host. hub2 is reserved for the control plane, documentation,
internal services, and homelab coordination.

- **Parking** was converged onto Trevarn and the legacy hub2 stack
  **decommissioned (2026-06-11)** — see the [Smart Parking (decommissioned)](../../services/parking.md)
  record and [Parking Convergence](../../services/trevarn/parking-convergence.md).
- **Occupancy** runs the incumbent `cbre_pipeline` on hub2 while the Trevarn
  converged pipeline proves parity in parallel-run; cutover is gated and not yet
  done.

This supersedes the earlier *"Consolidate Products to hub2"* decision (2026-02),
which co-located parking and occupancy on hub2; that consolidation is being
unwound in favour of the control-plane / customer-platform split.

## Metric definitions, baselines, and method

### M1 — CCM has exactly one canonical meaning *(keystone — solving it eases M2–M4)*
Baseline: **4** meanings in active use — (a) governance *contract* (`ccm.md`), (b) L1 *kernel-enforcement layer* (`authority-model` §3), (c) the *`ccm_edge_*` modules* (`authority-model` §3 L1), (d) informal *family of ccm-\* managers*.
Target: **1**. Recommended canonical statement: *"CCM = the CharlieHub Control Manager governance **contract**; the kernel enforcer is the **ccm-edge** subsystem."*
Method: grep every "CCM" definition; all but one resolve to the contract meaning. Requires operator decision (D1).
Owner: A2 (authority-model naming-collision fix) + A4.

**Ratified rule (2026-06-02) — auditable green-gate.** *If "CCM" refers to **work being performed**, name the subsystem that performs it (`ccm-edge` · `ccm-domain` · `ccm-transit` · `ccm-lan` …). If "CCM" refers to **governance, classification, ownership scope, lifecycle, compliance, or contract-derived concepts** — including terms-of-art like "CCM deployment model" — keep "CCM".* The test: *is the phrase naming a concept, or describing work?* M1 is **🟢** when: (1) CCM has exactly one meaning — the governance contract; (2) no canonical document uses CCM as a runtime actor; (3) every runtime action is attributed to a named subsystem; (4) contract-derived adjectives (`CCM-owned table`, `CCM-managed edge`, `CCM ownership record`, `CCM hooks`, `CCM source-rule`) remain valid; (5) historical records remain untouched.
**Closed 2026-06-02:** 45 actor-refs across 17 canonical docs → `ccm-edge`; validation sweep = **0** canonical CCM-as-actor (5 kept in historical `edge-convergence-audit-v1`). `CCM-Edge` name-styling (23×) is M10 cleanup, not an M1-meaning issue.

### M7 — Net reduction of architectural artifacts *(the program's pass/fail bar)*
The program must **end with fewer competing architectural artifacts than it began** — not "a few
new docs, maybe archive later." All four axes must move the right way: duplicated content (M3 ↓),
conflicting definitions (M2 → 0), concepts (M10 ↓), and **page count (same or fewer)**.

**Document categories** (every artifact is exactly one):

| Category | Examples | Fate |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Canonical authorities** | authority-model, doctrine, invariants, enforcement-model, ccm.md, architecture-map, subsystem service docs | survive |
| **2 — Transitional reconciliation artifacts** | boundary / reuse / convergence assessments, roadmap investigations, drift reports, *this charter* | archive · supersede · **absorb conclusions into Category 1**, then retire |
| **3 — Duplicated content blocks** | the 18 copies of 6 blocks (M3) | collapse to 6 homes + references |

**Hard rule (binding this sprint):** *a net-new canonical page must justify itself by retiring,
consolidating, or superseding multiple existing explanations.* Applied to live proposals:

| Architecture Reconciliation Charter | **Yes** (done) | replaced ad-hoc chat tracking; one tracker for the program |

### M9 — Domain Manager responsibility + naming *(clarification mandatory; rename optional)*
Lifecycle: **OPEN → RESPONSIBILITY CLARIFIED → (NAME RETAINED | NAME REPLACED)**. Responsibility
clarification is mandatory; the rename is optional and only follows from it.
One-sentence answer (already true post-A4): *"`charliehub_domain_manager_v3` is the hub2 control-plane service that hosts three subsystems — ccm-domain, ccm-edge, ccm-security — over the `charliehub_domains` database."* That sentence reads wrong for a service named "Domain Manager," which is the evidence-driven rename trigger.
Success: responsibility is canonical (CLARIFIED) **and** a naming decision is recorded — **either** name retained **with explicit justification** **or** a replacement selected. Failure: ambiguity left unresolved.
Gate (do not rename until): (1) hosting relation canonical in map + docs; (2) open movers resolved (does ccm-edge move? does ccm-security become a peer subsystem? does monitoring join?).
The A4 finding is **absorbed into `infrastructure/domain-manager.md`** (which today describes only
ccm-domain — the doc-level root of this confusion) + architecture-map; it is **not** a new page.

### M10 — Concept count *(the real target: cognitive load)*
The number of distinct architectural concepts an engineer must hold to reason about the control
plane. Baseline (seed, ~11 overlapping terms): CCM · ccm-domain · Domain Manager · ccm-edge ·
"CCM Edge"/"Edge Manager" · ccm-security · constrained-identities · CT2177 · architecture-map ·
crosswalk · authority-model. Many overlap — CCM carries 4 meanings; Domain-Manager vs ccm-domain;
Edge-Manager/CCM-Edge/ccm-edge is one thing under three names.
Target: **materially fewer** — collapse the redundant names and the 4 CCM meanings to 1.
Method: count distinct top-level terms a reader must disambiguate; a term with >1 meaning, or a
thing with >1 name, counts as separate load until collapsed. This is the outcome M1–M4 serve, and
the real objective behind "reduce competing explanations."

## Guardrails (binding)

- **Two-axis precedence.** *Fact-reconciliation* (drift): reality → service docs → architecture-map → crosswalk/authority prose → navigation. *Doctrinal* ([Authority Model §6.5](/control-plane/foundational/authority-model/)): Canonical Docs → Architecture Map → Assessments → Memory. They differ by question type: inventory/"what exists" → map leads; "who may write X" → Authority Model leads; "which doc do I open" → architecture-overview.
- Map = inventory/navigation authority; Authority Model = ownership-doctrine authority. Neither becomes the other (no 5th ownership matrix).
- **No new architectural authority sources may be created this sprint** — no fifth matrix, no second subsystem inventory, no second ownership model, no second architecture-map. The sprint *reconciles* authority; it does not *create* it.
- **Net-new canonical pages must retire / consolidate / supersede multiple existing explanations** to justify creation (M7). Default: absorb into an existing canonical doc rather than create a new one.
- No new concepts; consolidate before archiving; register conflicts (don't silently resolve); mark uncertain items **EVIDENCE MISSING**.

## Sprint 1 architectural outcomes

The durable result of Sprint 1 is not the edit / duplicate / delink counts (audit history in the change log) — it is the set of decisions that will still matter in 12 months:

1. **CCM has exactly one meaning** — the governance *contract*; runtime actions belong to named subsystems (M1 🟢).
2. **Domain Manager's responsibility is explicit** — `charliehub_domain_manager_v3` *hosts* ccm-domain + ccm-edge + ccm-security; it is not "just domains" (D1).
3. **ccm-security is a peer subsystem** (D3) — own intent (schema · API · renderer · invariant), realized at the edge through a documented `ccm-security → ccm-edge` handoff.
4. **Authelia's dependency footprint is enumerable** (M11) — rules-block → Domain Manager · WAN-IP → wan-watcher · mechanism → Authority Model §5.2 · artifact → `configuration.yml`; framed as a *consumer* of CharlieHub-generated state (migration-ready).
5. **Architecture-map = inventory / navigation authority only** — what exists and where.
6. **Authority Model = ownership authority only** — who may write.

The two-authority separation (#5 / #6) is the structural guardrail the rest of the program depends on.

## 1. Purpose

This document defines the authority model of the CharlieHub infrastructure. It answers one question only:

> For any mutable system state: who is the single writer?

This is the canonical reference for:

- ownership boundaries
- control-plane layering
- drift detection expectations
- future consolidation work

---

## 2. Core Principle

**Every mutable state has exactly one authoritative writer.**

Corollaries:

- No shared writes
- No implicit ownership
- No "temporary" dual control
- Exceptions must be explicit and documented

---

## 3. Control Plane Layers

The system is organised into strictly separated layers.

### L0 — Observation Layer

- **Component:** lan-watcher
- **Responsibility:** Collect infrastructure metadata — device presence, ARP/DHCP, MAC/IP mapping — and project it into `infrastructure_assets`.
- **Properties:** Read-only relative to kernel/WG state. No side effects on other layers. Feeds higher layers.

### L1 — Kernel Enforcement Layer (ccm-edge)

- **Component:** ccm-edge (edge-local kernel enforcement subsystem — `ccm_edge_*` modules, hosted in the Domain Manager service). *"CCM" is the governance contract (CharlieHub Control Manager), not a writer — see [CCM](ccm.md).*
- **Responsibility:** Apply kernel state — nftables, `ip rule`, routing tables — and ensure convergence to declared state.
- **Properties:** Only writer of kernel networking state. Idempotent application. Derives from upstream declarations; does not invent topology.

### L2 — Fabric Definition Layer

- **Component:** Transit Manager (Transit Manager)
- **Responsibility:** Define transport topology — WireGuard interfaces, peers (managed set), addressing, policy intent. Generate desired state for ccm-edge.
- **Properties:** No direct kernel writes. No NAT ownership (post-2026-04-22). Declarative render model (DB → render).

### L3 — External Peer Layer

- **Component:** transit-manager (hub2) — absorbed from vpn-wg-manager (CT1119, stopped 2026-04-24)
- **Responsibility:** Manage dynamic peers — road warriors (`wg-rw`), outposts, external clients — and generate WireGuard client `.conf` files (US UCG GEO exit is the only remaining on-device config consumer).
- **Properties:** Peer lifecycle managed via transit-manager API (`/api/vpn/peers`). `wg-rw` interface config remains a standalone wg-quick unit on transit-core, outside the standard render-deploy cycle — see §5.1.

### LA — Application Control Plane

- **Component:** Domain Manager
- **Responsibility:** DNS, Traefik routing, Authelia rules (partial), user provisioning, ACME / TLS.
- **Properties:** DB-backed. Generator-driven. No kernel interaction.

### LA-aux — Auxiliary Control Plane

- **Component:** wan-watcher
- **Responsibility:** WAN state observation; writes specific config fragments (Authelia WAN-IP section, Traefik allowlists).
- **Properties:** Narrow scope. Must not overlap ownership domains.

## 5. Explicit Exceptions

### 5.1 wg-rw (road warrior VPN)

- Interface config (`/etc/wireguard/wg-rw.conf`) remains a **standalone wg-quick systemd unit** on ch-transit-core, outside Transit Manager's render-deploy cycle. Transit Manager's deploy set covers the standard fabric interfaces (for the current set query the Transit Manager API / see [WireGuard VPN](../../network/fabric-v2/wireguard.md); note `wg-us` was renamed `wga-usa`, and `wg-outpost` was retired 2026-07-02) — **`wg-rw` is excluded** (its peers are managed directly on transit-core). *(Interface list de-inlined 2026-07-20 — verified against the Transit Manager API; do not re-hardcode the deploy set here.)*
- **Peers managed by transit-manager** via `/api/vpn/peers` (road warriors, outpost, infra, and contractor peers — query the live roster; counts change frequently). Absorbed from vpn-wg-manager (CT1119, stopped 2026-04-24, Phase 2.5).
- Transit Manager integrity service marks `wg-rw` as `unmanaged` for the interface shell — the render returns `null` for this interface; its pubkey, listen port, and address are outside Transit Manager's deploy scope. Peer lifecycle IS managed.

**Rationale:** hybrid model. The interface shell is static (standalone wg-quick config, unchanged since initial provisioning). The peer set is dynamic and managed by transit-manager's VPN peer API. This avoids the full render-deploy cycle for peer additions/removals while keeping the interface config stable.

### 5.2 Authelia dual-writer — verified 2026-04-22

Both services hold `rw` bind-mounts on `/opt/charliehub/authelia/config` and write to the same `configuration.yml`.

- **Writer 1 — Domain Manager** (`charliehub_domain_manager_v3`): generates the managed access-rules block from the `domains` table. Rewrites large portions of the file on regeneration.
- **Writer 2 — wan-watcher** (`charliehub_wan_watcher`, `wan_watcher.py::update_authelia_config()`): patches **three specific `/32` lines** inside the file using regex substitution, keyed on YAML **comment anchors**:

    ```
    - <IP>/32   # ... UK ... WAN ...
    - <IP>/32   # ... FR ... WAN ...
    - <IP>/32   # ... Paris ... WAN ...   (optional)
    ```

    If the regex matches, the IP is replaced with the current WAN IP. wan-watcher then **restarts the Authelia container via Docker API** (`container.restart(timeout=30)`). Domain Manager issues its own restart trigger on regeneration.

- **Coupling model:** not section-based. wan-watcher locates its three targets by *comment text*, not by managed markers. Domain Manager must preserve those exact comment strings across regenerations or wan-watcher silently fails to match.

**Risks — all live as of v1.1:**

1. **Comment-keyed regex is fragile.** If Domain Manager's authelia generator ever rewrites the comment format, wan-watcher logs `"Authelia config unchanged, no restart needed"` (not an error, no alert) and WAN IPs silently become stale. No integrity check exists for this.
2. **Concurrent-write race.** wan-watcher pattern is read → regex → write. Domain Manager can regenerate between read and write; wan-watcher's write would clobber DM's change. No file-level lock.
3. **Double restart.** Both writers restart Authelia independently on their own schedule. If they fire close together the container flaps.

**Status:** documented exception. See §9.3 for target direction — eliminating this dual-writer is tracked.

## 6. Invariants

### 6.1 Layer separation

- Transit Manager never writes kernel state.
- ccm-edge never invents topology.
- Domain Manager never touches networking kernel state.

### 6.2 Single-writer rule

Every resource must map to exactly one writer. Exceptions must be:

- documented (§5)
- intentional (not accidental)
- bounded (with a path to resolution)

### 6.3 Render → apply model

All managed state must follow:

```
Database → Generator → Artifact → ccm-edge apply
```

No direct mutation of:

- kernel state
- generated files
- runtime configs

### 6.4 Drift visibility

- Drift must be detectable.
- Drift must be attributable to a specific layer.
- No silent correction without signal.

### 6.5 Documentation authority precedence

The authority matrix (§4) answers "who writes this *state*?" This subsection
answers the adjacent question: **when two sources describe the same decision and
disagree, which one wins?** Authority resolves in a fixed order — lower never
overrides higher:

```
Canonical Documentation   (docs.charliehub.net — this site)
        ↓
Architecture Map          (architecture-map.yaml)
        ↓
Program Assessments       (published analysis / decision docs)
        ↓
Agent / session memory    (navigation aid only)
```

- **Canonical documentation** is the top authority for a ratified decision.
- The **architecture map** is authoritative for *navigation* — subsystem
  ownership, source-of-truth boundaries, generator ownership — but defers to
  canonical docs on the *substance* of a ratified decision.
- **Program assessments** are evidence and analysis. They justify decisions and
  may be cited, but do not by themselves ratify them.
- **Memory is a navigation aid, not an authority.** Memory may help *locate* a
  decision, but cannot *establish, modify, supersede, or ratify* one.

This extends the two existing precedence rules already in force: documentation
wins over `CLAUDE.md`, and the architecture map is the authoritative navigation
source.

### 6.6 Decision durability

A **durable architectural decision** — new doctrine, a new invariant, an
architecture decision, a new anti-pattern, a governance change, or program
creation — MUST live in canonical documentation. It may be *pointed to* from
memory or an assessment, but must not *survive only* there. A memory-only durable
decision is a governance manifestation of the
[Shadow Inventory](/control-plane/foundational/shadow-inventory.md) anti-pattern:
a second, informal source of truth that diverges silently from the canonical
one.

Operating rule — every durable conclusion that outlives a session is **either**:

1. published immediately to its canonical destination, **or**
2. recorded as a **pending-documentation item** carrying an explicit **owner +
   destination document + trigger condition**.

It is never left as a bare note. Temporary working notes and program *status
markers* ("program X is active", "doctrine fragment held for soak") may remain
memory-only; findings and decisions may not.

## 7. Drift Model

### Detection

- **Transit Manager drift metrics:** fabric integrity (peer count, routes, config hash, nft hash, tunnel liveness).
- **Domain Manager drift checks:** routing/DNS (`/api/dns/status`, `/api/control-plane/health`).
- **ccm-edge convergence checks:** planned extension — currently covered by read-only cron scripts.

### Classification

| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Structural drift | missing route, interface absent |
| State drift | wrong `ip rule`, wrong NAT target |
| Ownership drift | resource modified by the wrong writer |

Reference: [three-layer drift-control model (hook / cron / network)](https://docs.charliehub.net/control-plane/foundational/enforcement-model/) — detection crons never auto-fix.

- The `proto 99` marker for vpn-wg-manager-owned routes is **not currently used**. Live state on transit-core, px1, and px5 shows zero routes with `proto 99`.

- For v1.1 this is removed from the live authority claims. It remains an optional future mechanism, not a current invariant.

## 9. Target Direction

### 9.1 ccm-edge as universal kernel enforcer

All kernel state converges under ccm-edge:

- nftables ✓ (done)
- `ip rule` ✓ (done)
- routing ✓ (done)
- interface state (future)

### 9.2 Strict layer contracts

- Transit Manager → declarative intent only
- ccm-edge → enforcement only
- No cross-layer mutation

### 9.3 Eliminate dual writers

- Authelia → single writer (resolve §5.2 by either (a) wan-watcher emits an input file that Domain Manager consumes, or (b) Authelia config is regenerated atomically with both inputs).
- WAN state → read-only input to the generator, not a direct config writer.

## 11. Terminology

Locked vocabulary for cross-document consistency:

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Writer** | The single service authorised to mutate a given resource. |
| **Render** | Deterministic, side-effect-free generation of desired state from a source-of-truth DB. |
| **Apply** | The act of converging live state to match rendered state. Only performed by the resource's writer. |
| **Authority** | The layer that owns a resource's render → apply cycle. |
| **Drift** | Any divergence between rendered state and live state, detectable by a reader. |
| **Managed gap** | A resource deliberately outside a given writer's scope, explicitly documented (e.g. `wg-rw` under Transit Manager). Not a bug. |
| **CCM** | The CharlieHub Control Manager governance *contract* over all control-plane components (see [CCM](ccm.md)). Not a service, subsystem, or writer. |
| **ccm-edge** | The subsystem with authority for edge-local kernel enforcement (NAT, policy routing, interface realization, WAN runtime); the concrete writer of kernel state. "CCM" (the contract) must not be used to name this enforcer. |

# Gateway Convergence Doctrine v1

**Lifecycle:** REFERENCE
<!-- lifecycle: REFERENCE -->


*Last updated: 2026-05-29*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ACTIVE DOCTRINE |
| **Authority** | Normative |
| **Applies to** | All CharlieHub gateways; Control Plane (CCM Edge, Transit Manager, Domain Manager) |
| **Sibling doctrine** | [CCM Contract](ccm.md), [SD-WAN Architecture](../sdwan.md), [Transit Edge Spec](../specs/transit-edge-spec.md) |

---

## Core Principle

**Gateway identity is logical. Hardware is disposable.**

CharlieHub does not distinguish between "provisioning" and "repair."

All gateways exist on a single convergence path toward declared desired state.

The control plane owns the canonical definition of a gateway and continuously
moves runtime reality toward that definition.

Provisioning is merely the special case where runtime state starts empty.

Repair is merely the special case where runtime state has drifted.

Replacement is merely the special case where identity persists but hardware
changes.

---

## Design Principle

There MUST be one convergence engine.

There MUST NOT be separate systems for:

- new gateway onboarding
- replacement gateway deployment
- gateway repair / drift correction

These are different entry states into the same lifecycle.

---

## The Three Supported Scenarios

### Scenario 1 — New Site + New Gateway

Example:

- new US GEO exit
- new remote office

Starting state:

- blank compatible hardware

Outcome:

- site created
- gateway staged
- gateway activated
- production state converged

**Classification:** `GREENFIELD`

---

### Scenario 2 — Existing Site + New Gateway

Example:

- replacing fr-edge-1 hardware
- Pi4 → Optiplex migration
- failed appliance replacement

Starting state:

- existing site
- existing edge identity
- replacement hardware

Outcome:

- hardware claims existing gateway identity
- staging validation
- cutover
- production convergence

Important:

- Gateway identity persists.
- Hardware is fungible.

**Classification:** `REPLACEMENT`

---

### Scenario 3 — Existing Site + Existing Gateway Drift

Example:

- manual fail2ban debt
- resolver divergence
- bootstrap artifacts
- legacy nic1.cfg

Starting state:

- operational gateway
- partial divergence from control plane

Outcome:

- drift detected
- staged reconciliation
- convergence toward doctrine

Important:

- No reinstall required.

**Classification:** `RECONCILIATION`

---

## Convergence Principle

Every gateway MUST be representable as:

```
desired_state - actual_state = convergence_work
```

The starting point differs by scenario.

The engine does not.

---

## Gateway Lifecycle

All gateways move through explicit lifecycle states:

- `unclaimed`
- `staging`
- `validated`
- `active`
- `maintenance`
- `replacement`
- `retired`

Lifecycle transitions MUST be explicit and observable.

---

## Platform Doctrine

Compatible hardware platforms are implementation details.

Examples:

- Raspberry Pi 4
- Dell Optiplex 3050

The control plane MUST be platform-aware but platform-agnostic.

Site identity MUST survive hardware replacement.

A compatible gateway should be able to move between sites with only a
site-specific bootstrap transition.

Example:

> A Paris Pi4 should be capable of becoming a Dinard gateway after
> identity reassignment and site-specific activation.

---

## Staging Doctrine

CharlieHub SHALL maintain a canonical gateway staging environment.

**Reserved subnet:** `10.11.0.0/16`

Purpose:

- validate gateways before site deployment
- validate replacement hardware
- test convergence logic safely
- prove LAN-side behaviour before WAN cutover

Staging MUST resemble production.

Temporary gateway behaviour in staging SHOULD be as production-like as possible.

**Future enhancement:** virtualized WAN simulation (ONT emulator) for WAN `nic0` testing.

---

## Control Plane Principle

The control plane MUST own:

- desired gateway identity
- networking intent
- resolver intent
- trust/security policy
- routing intent
- execution role
- hardware profile
- lifecycle state

A single control-plane API MUST be sufficient to create, repair, replace, or
converge any compatible gateway.

---

## Estate-Driven Architecture Principle

New abstractions MUST emerge from observed estate reality.

**The running estate is the oracle.**

Requirements MUST be harvested from:

- Paris
- Dinard
- UK
- existing bootstrap debt
- deployment history
- operational incidents
- historical divergence

Avoid speculative abstractions.

If a model does not elegantly support:

1. new site + new gateway
2. existing site + new gateway
3. existing site + existing gateway drift

then the model is incomplete.

*Navigation layer: operational question → authority → source of truth → API → consumer.*

This document is the primary entry point for any CharlieHub operational or debugging question.
Start here before opening SSH, grep-ing config files, or reading implementation code.

## Global Invariants

The CCM contract is defined canonically in **[CCM Contract](/control-plane/foundational/ccm.md)**. The summary
below is kept only because the crosswalk is the operational entry point for authority decisions:

- **I-1** — DB is the only source of truth.
- **I-2** — API is the only write path. **Direct SQL is break-glass only, justified and documented.**
- **I-3** — Generators overwrite entirely; exactly one component owns each artifact path.
- **I-4** — Deploy can lag; a DB commit is not rolled back by runtime.
- **I-5** — Every entity has an explicit lifecycle state (`draft` / `active` / `inactive` / `planned`).

## Operational Questions

### "Is this hostname/domain managed here? Who owns its routing?"

**Authority:** Domain Manager (ccm-domain)
**Source of truth:** `charliehub_domains.domains`

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/domains?domain=<name>" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
```

Response gives you: `backend_host` (must be a static IP — never an FQDN), `backend_port`,
`auth_required`, `service_type`, `tls_mode`.

- `service_type='static'` → DNS-only record; Traefik skips it entirely
- `service_type='http'` → live backend with Traefik route

---

### "What WireGuard interfaces exist and what are their geo assignments?"

**Authority:** Transit Manager · **Source of truth:** `transit.interfaces`, `transit.geos`

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/interfaces" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_API_KEY" | jq '.[] | {name, geo_table_id, status, interface_type}'
```

Geo table IDs: 201=uk, 202=fr, 203=us, 204=ad. `geo_table_id=null` → not a GEO executor.
Never edit `/etc/wireguard/wg-*.conf` directly — rendered state.

---

### "What NAT rules are deployed to edge X? Is anything drifted?"

**Authority:** CCM Edge · **Source of truth:** `ccm.nat_rules WHERE edge_id=X`

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges/6/nat" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges/6/consistency" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
```

Edge IDs (canonical: [ccm-edge §Edges](/services/ccm-edge/#edges)): uk-edge-1=6, fr-edge-1=7, paris-edge-pi4=3. (uk-staging=10 decommissioned 2026-06-12.)

---

### "What geo does device X exit through? How do I change it?"

**Authority:** Transit Manager · **Source of truth:** `transit.routing_overrides` or `transit.peers.geo`

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/routing-overrides/10.35.50.50" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"geo": "uk", "name": "Office TV"}'

# Fast path for WG peer (no full deploy needed):
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/peers/42/apply-geo" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"geo": "fr"}'
```

---

### "Is edge X registered? Can it be deployed to?"

Two checks required — TM and CCM are independent:

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/edge-nodes" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_API_KEY" | jq '.[] | select(.hostname=="uk-edge-1") | {id, status, execution_capable, wan_type}'
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | jq '.[] | select(.node_hostname=="uk-edge-1") | {id, state}'
```

**Both must be `active`.** I-CCM-1: active CCM edge requires active TM node.

---

### "Why did deploy-transit skip edge X?"

Check in order — all answers are in DB/API, not on the edge:

1. `TM edge_node.status ≠ 'active'` → excluded from apply_order. Never reached.
2. TCP reachability probe failed (3 s to mgmt_ip) → SKIP_NODES, continue.
3. TRANSPORT_RISKY + WAN gate: edge has no non-WG route to hub2 → SKIP.
4. Paris-specific quarantine: wg-paris stale (>180 s) → quarantine script required.

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/deploy" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_API_KEY" | jq 'sort_by(.deployed_at) | last'
```

---

### "Which deploy path should I use — deploy-transit.sh or POST /api/transit/deploy?"

**Two distinct surfaces.** Evidence is in `transit.edge_node_status.delivery_transport`.

| Surface | Transport | `delivery_transport` |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|
| `deploy-transit.sh` | SSH + SCP | `'wan_recovery'` or NULL |
| `POST /api/transit/deploy` | edge-agent HTTP :8091 (wg-site overlay) | `'overlay'` |

Check which path is appropriate before running:

```sql
SELECT en.hostname, en.wan_type, ens.delivery_transport,
  (en.last_apply_transport_snapshot IS NULL) as never_deployed
FROM transit.edge_nodes en
LEFT JOIN transit.edge_node_status ens ON ens.edge_node_id = en.id
WHERE en.status = 'active';
```

`delivery_transport='overlay'` → edge-agent HTTP preferred.
`NULL` or `'wan_recovery'` → SSH path or manual bypass for first deploy (see [Bootstrap Authority Map](/control-plane/specs/bootstrap-authority-map.md)).

---

### "Is this service on edge X managed by CCM, or is it manual/native?"

**Authority:** `ccm.edge_services` — the edge service ownership inventory.

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges/7/services" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
```

| `owner` | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `'ccm_edge'` | Generated and managed by CCM. Touching directly is a drift event. |
| `'manual'` | CCM tracks but does not generate. Human-maintained. |
| `'proxmox_native'` | Proxmox structural service. Do not interfere. |

Note: as of 2026-06-30 (re-verified) this table has no rows for active production edges. The API and schema are live but unpopulated for production. Only px5-lemans (id=1, edge role retired) has rows.

---

### "What security profile applies to edge X? What CIDRs are operator-trusted?"

**Authority:** CCM Security (`ccm_security.*`, Domain Manager `/api/ccm/security/*`)

This is a **separate subsystem** from CCM Edge. It manages:
- `ccm_security.trust_boundaries` (23 rows): CIDR → trust class
- `ccm_security.operator_sources`: MAC/pubkey/CIDR → current operator IP (freshness-tracked)
- `ccm_security.security_profiles`: edge → profile (transitional-edge / hardened-wan-edge / canonical-edge-track-a)

Hard-fail rule: renderer aborts if any active operator source fails to resolve.

| trust_class | ban_allowed | recovery_allowed |
|---|---|---|
| `operator`, `authoritative`, `execution`, `control_plane_transit` | false | **true** |
| `constrained`, `unknown` | **true** | false |

Missing security profile for an active edge blocks Phase F (security deploy). Fix: insert a row into `ccm_security.security_profiles`.

---

### "Can I edit a value in a deployed config file directly?"

**No.** Files under `/etc/wireguard/`, `/etc/network/ccm-hooks/`, `/etc/dnsmasq.d/` with a `# Generated by` header are rendered state. Direct edits are overwritten on next deploy.

Correct path: change the DB record via the owning API → deploy.

Invariant I-3: generators overwrite entirely.

---

### "Which database holds the source of truth?"

`charliehub-postgres` container on hub2.

| Schema | Owner service |
|--------|--------------|
| `transit.*` | Transit Manager |
| `ccm.*` + `ccm_security.*` | CCM Edge / CCM Security (via Domain Manager API) |
| `charliehub_domains.*` | Domain Manager |
| `docs.*` | Docs Manager |
| `public.ccm_lan_*` | CCM-LAN (NOTE: not `ccm.*` — historical schema placement) |
| `infrastructure_assets` | LAN Watcher |
| `mail.*` | Mail API |

Never write directly except as documented break-glass.

## Key Workflows

### deploy-transit (5 phases)

```
Phase 0: ccm-edge pre-render (active CCM edges only)
Phase 1: For each TM-active edge in apply_order:
          TCP probe → transport class (SAFE=syncconf / RISKY=restart+WAN-gate) → apply
Phase 2: transit-core apply via SSH ForceCommand
Phase 3: convergence wait (WG handshake polling)
Phase 4: fabric assertion (check_transit_fabric.sh --quick)
Phase 5: ccm-edge reconcile (active CCM edges only)
```

Rollback triggers **only** on Phase 2 failure. Edge failures are non-fatal.

**Pre-deploy transport check:**

```sql
SELECT en.hostname, en.wan_type, ens.delivery_transport,
  (en.last_apply_transport_snapshot IS NULL) as never_deployed
FROM transit.edge_nodes en
LEFT JOIN transit.edge_node_status ens ON ens.edge_node_id = en.id
WHERE en.status = 'active';
```

### CCM Edge deploy

```bash
source /opt/charliehub/.env
# Dry run first (always safe):
curl -s -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges/6/deploy?dry_run=true' \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
# Live deploy:
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/ccm/edge/edges/6/deploy \
  -H "X-API-Key: $DOMAIN_MANAGER_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
```

Edge IDs (canonical: [ccm-edge §Edges](/services/ccm-edge/#edges)): uk-edge-1=6, fr-edge-1=7, paris-edge-pi4=3. (uk-staging=10 decommissioned 2026-06-12.)

### Edge onboarding ceremony

```
B1 site subnet (SQL) → B2 TM node (draft) → B3 WG peer → B4 VLAN profile (optional)
B5 CCM edge (draft) → B6 NAT rules → B7 CCM activate (REQUIRES A10 bilateral SSH trust)
B8 TM activate → Phase C (first deploy) → Phase E (ccm-edge deploy) → Phase F (security)
```

B7 runs SSH preflight from the DM container. Returns 502 without A10 trust.

The CharlieHub Control Plane is the governance architecture for all infrastructure
management. It defines **what must always be true** (invariants), **who is the sole
writer** of each resource (authority model), and **how writes are enforced**
(enforcement layers). Every managed service — Domain Manager, Transit Manager, CCM
Edge, CCM LAN, Docs API — implements the same contract.
